Appendix 2 — AD&D Game Conversions

When moving characters between the two games, convert levels, not experience points. Levels 1-12 transfer unchanged. Above that, one AD&D level equals three BECMI levels going one way, and three BECMI levels equal one AD&D level going the other; round fractions down. Multiclass AD&D characters use the level of the active class, and dual-class characters use their active class.

Keep Lawful-Neutral-Chaotic as a role-playing axis when converting to BECMI; assign Good-Neutral-Evil from past behavior when converting to AD&D. Use equivalent spells where they exist and assume knowledge is lost where no equivalent exists. Ordinary equipment, encumbrance and money are converted by using the target game's tables; adjust the starting purse so it fits the treasure level of the new campaign.

A shield gives -1 AC in both systems. Weapon mastery of Expert or better converts to the target game's weapon proficiency; demihuman multiclass options that have no BECMI equivalent should be approved by the DM case by case.
